claim_verdicts.evidence: refs/tags/stage-0 is the annotated tag object 664d38a; its `object` field is commit ff911b0, which is the checked-out head of branch auto/stage-0, so the working tree is the tag. Smells.cs line 8-9: `public static int ShippingVnd(` / `int totalVnd, bool express, bool loyal, bool pickUp, string city, int weightGram)` — six parameters on line 9. `loyal` occurs nowhere else in lines 10-30. Executed grid (576 inputs, SDK 10.0.300): flipping only `loyal` never changed the result (loyal_changes_price=0).

Line 18 `if (totalVnd < 2000000) return express ? 60000 : 30000;` is reached only through `if (!pickUp)` (11), `if (city == "Hà Nội" || city == "Hồ Chí Minh")` (13) and `if (weightGram < 5000)` (15), and is itself the fourth `if`, whose body is that return. So the first prices returned by the method sit inside four nested `if` statements.

Line 17 is `// charge 30000 unless the total reaches 2000000`; line 18 is `if (totalVnd < 2000000) return express ? 60000 : 30000;`. Executed with the verbatim body on SDK 10.0.300: Hồ Chí Minh, express, 1000 g, total 1_000_000 returns 60000. The comment text contains neither `express` nor 60000.

Lines 18-19: `if (totalVnd < 2000000) return express ? 60000 : 30000;` and `return express ? 60000 : 0;` at 20 spaces of indent. Lines 22-23 are the same two statements at 16 spaces; no other character differs. The lesson's code block (lines=8-30) is character-for-character the file at the tag.

`weightGram` is read only on line 15, and both branches of that check hold identical statements (claim 4). Executed on SDK 10.0.300 with the stage-0 body copied verbatim over totals {0, 999_999, 1_000_000, 1_999_999, 2_000_000, 5_000_000} x express x loyal x pickUp x {Hà Nội, Hồ Chí Minh, Đà Nẵng} x weights {0, 4999, 5000, 10000} = 576 inputs: changing only weightGram (0 vs 10000) never changed the result (weight_changes_price=0).

C# reference, const keyword: "A constant expression is an expression that the compiler can fully evaluate at compile time" and "because compilers propagate constants, other code compiled with your libraries needs to be recompiled to see the changes" — the value is fixed at compile time and substituted where it is used. Executed: the version with 2000000 and each price replaced by `const int` names of the same value agreed with the original on all 576 inputs (step3_diffs=0).

"The `//` starts a **comment** in C#. Comments are any text you want to keep in your source code but don't execute as code. The compiler doesn't generate any executable code from comments." The comments reference names the only comments the compiler does read: "Some comments start with three slashes: `///`. … The compiler reads these comments to produce human documentation." No page describes any comparison of `//` text with nearby code.

Lines 18 and 22 each carry their own `2000000` literal, on the two sides of the line-15 weight check. Executed: a copy with line 18's limit changed to 1000000 and line 22's left at 2000000 differed from the original on 16 of the 576 inputs — exactly the delivered Hà Nội / Hồ Chí Minh standard orders with totals between the two limits, at weights below 5000 (oneLimitChanged_diffs=16).

Definition of a vocab term this lesson introduces: content/glossary.yaml `refactoring`, short_en "Changing structure without changing behavior, in small steps", introduced_in foundation.l1.code-smells-basic. No docs root in content/versions.yaml defines the term, and a definition the lesson itself sets needs no external source.

Definition of the other vocab term: glossary `code-smell`, short_en "A surface sign of a deeper design problem". The five smells named match outline item 1 of this lesson in track.yaml (duplicated code, long parameter lists, comments explaining what, magic numbers, deep nesting), and the file header comment of Smells.cs lists the same five.

Tautological once claim 15 fixes the term: a step that moved a result did not preserve behaviour, so it was not a refactoring. The lesson states it with its condition ("If any result moved"), not as an unconditioned rule, so no external source applies.

The checkable half holds: ShippingVnd has six `return` statements (lines 18, 19, 22, 23, 26, 29) and five `? :` (18, 19, 22, 23, 26), and the input set the lesson describes — totals just below and at 2000000, on both sides of the weight check, with and without express, plus another city and pick-up — reaches all six returns and both sides of all five `? :`; the executed grid contains exactly those inputs. The rest ("small enough to hold in your head") is advice given with its condition.

A value judgement carrying its own condition ("when you are about to read and edit the code anyway"), matching outline item 4 of this lesson in track.yaml. No docs root in versions.yaml covers when to refactor; there is no factual assertion to source and no unconditioned always/never.

Tautological as written: one comparison of end results gives one answer covering all edits together, so that comparison alone cannot attribute a difference to one edit. The lesson's wording matches the claim's strength ("the check shows that a price moved but not which edit moved it").

`loyal` occurs only in the signature (line 9) and weightGram never changes a result (weight_changes_price=0 over 576 executed inputs), so both smells are equally consistent with today's prices being right and with a rule planned and never written. Nothing in Smells.cs states an intended price and no test covers the method at stage-0 (claim 6), so reading alone cannot settle which.

First half holds: lines 18 and 22 carry bare `2000000` literals, no identifier names the value, only the line-17 comment mentions it. Second half misses a condition: lines 19, 23 and 26 all sit inside `if (!pickUp)` (line 11) and line 29 returns 0 for every pick-up order. Executed: Đà Nẵng, pick-up, standard, total 100_000 returns 0, not 45000. So "free from 2000000 only for Hà Nội and Hồ Chí Minh" and "other cities pay 45000 standard or 90000 express at any total" are true of delivered orders only. The lesson body states only the first half, so no lesson sentence is affected.
